status_change_note.append_only_declaration: APPEND ONLY. Every field above this note records what happened DURING the 2026-07-31 acquisition run and is unchanged. The single field modified anywhere in this manifest is snapshot_status, which is an assessment of the run rather than a record of it. The snapshot's files were not touched.
status_change_note.why_not_failed: The data was genuine; the verification was absent. 'failed' would be as inaccurate as 'complete' - it would assert this run retrieved bad data, which is not what happened and not what the evidence shows.
status_change_note.why_the_original_complete_was_not_earned: The 'complete' status was assigned by scripts/external_sources/scunpacked_com.py as it stood on 2026-07-31, whose main() returned None and therefore exited 0 unconditionally. No endpoint outcome could ever have failed that run. The script also wrote every response body to its final filename BEFORE examining resp.status_code, so an HTTP error page would have been saved as ships.json and reported as a successful landing. The status describes what the script always said, not what was checked.

superseded_by.content_relationship: byte-identical - matching SHA-256 AND matching ETag on both endpoints
superseded_by.gates: all five passed in order (files present, JSON parses, file-type inspection, malware scan, content-indicator scan), with the malware scan preceding the rename out of .partial

status_change_note.what_byte_identity_does_and_does_not_est: Byte-identity confirms the bytes in THIS snapshot are genuine upstream bytes - the same content api served to an independently verified run. It does NOT retroactively verify this run. Nothing performed in 2026-07-31 checked anything; the confidence comes entirely from 20260801T042157Z. This snapshot is trustworthy by inheritance, not by its own process.
status_change_note.clarification_on_report_only_mode_confir: This manifest's integrity_scan.malware_scan.report_only_mode_confirmed is false. That value is correct as written and stays. It records that Set-MpPreference failed with 'You don't have enough permissions to perform the requested operation' because the PowerShell session was not elevated - it does NOT record a scan failure. The scan itself ran and returned no threats. The superseding run avoids the issue entirely by passing -DisableRemediation on the MpCmdRun scan command, which requires no elevation.
status_change_note.vocabulary_note: See status_vocabulary_reference below. At the time of this append, the project had no single canonical definition of the snapshot_status vocabulary anywhere in docs/ or code - the values existed only as strings used across manifests. That gap is recorded rather than papered over.

status_vocabulary_reference.definition_of_superseded: superseded - the data is genuine, but the run's verification cannot be trusted; a later verified run replaces it.
